title: Exposure wheel
description: A knurled exposure ring changes the brightness of an architectural photograph in precise one-third-stop increments.
useCase: Compact relative scrubbing controls for photographic adjustments, with a fixed index and immediate visual feedback.
interaction: Drag the wheel or adjust exposure with arrow keys.
reducedMotion: The wheel, index and photograph respond immediately to all input; no inertial or automatic motion runs.
limitations: The sample JPEG-derived WebP is multiplied with CSS brightness using 2^EV. This is a display approximation, not linear RAW exposure processing; clipped image detail cannot be recovered. Sample photograph is separately licensed under Unsplash.
look: Dark graphite camera body with a black-and-white architectural photo and a knurled tick-scale wheel with an amber index, on a flat burnt-orange background.
motion: Dragging the wheel horizontally slides its knurl and tick scale under a fixed amber index, snapping to one-third stops while the photo's brightness follows 2^EV; arrow keys step instantly.
adapt: Drag mapping is in `onPointerMove` (54 px per stop; `limit` snaps to thirds and clamps ±3), and `ev` drives the strip offsets and the `brightness` filter. Replace the image `src` and point `ev` at your own setting.
